chunk.note: one demo3 `characterization` chunk, emitted by demo3's own patch emitter at demo3's seed, so the traced geometry is the geometry the committed record traced

closure_against_committed_record.note: the committed stage timer brackets the whole `trace_ray_batch` call per chunk, which is what `reconstructed_as_committed` reconstructs. Agreement here is what licenses reading the fractions above as fractions of the 98.96 s rather than of a probe's own workload.

consequence: The lever is the wavelength handoff, not the chunk size, not the precision, and not the ray count. `RayBundle.wavelength_m` is a scalar by contract, so the per-ray array was N copies of one number; a size-1 array traces bitwise identically and is what `trace_ray_batch` now ships. After it the trace stage is ~3 s of demo3 rather than 99 s, and the emitter (M5.2) becomes the binding constraint.

optiland_material_index_cache_key.attribution: the difference between the two wavelength arms, which differ in nothing else. Corroborated independently by timing the lookups: 16 lookups at the measured per-call cost predict 0.3011 s against 0.3114 s measured
optiland_material_index_cache_key.what: host-side construction and hashing of optiland's refractive-index cache key. `BaseMaterial._create_cache_key` evaluates `tuple(np.ravel(be.to_numpy(wavelength)))`, so a per-ray wavelength array is copied to the host and turned into an 200000-element Python tuple, 16 times per chunk

optiland_ray_geometry_kernels.attribution: the size-1-wavelength arm, which does no cache-key work
optiland_ray_geometry_kernels.what: the trace itself: surface intersection, aperture clip, refraction, optical-path accumulation, and `_record_real`'s copy of eight full-length arrays per surface

repository_side_handoff.attribution: the shipped call minus the solver trace it contains
repository_side_handoff.what: everything `trace_ray_batch` does around the solver call: |a|^2, the launch-plane check, the two `bridge_arrays` conversions, the clipped-ray mask, and one host synchronization to count clipped rays

finding: Of the reconstructed 324.6 ms per 200 k-ray chunk, 95.9% is optiland building and hashing a Python tuple of the wavelength array, 1.6% is the ray geometry it exists to compute, and 2.5% is this repository's handoff. The cost is uniform per surface -- the spherical surface's intersection solve is not distinguishable from the planes -- because the dominant term is per-surface material lookups, not geometry.

handoff_breakdown_s.note: individually measured pieces, NOT a partition of the bucket. A piece timed on its own can cost differently in place: JAX dispatches asynchronously, and an array a previous piece already realized is cheaper for the next one to read. `closure_ratio` is how far that goes here. Reported because after CHE-118's fix this bucket is the majority of the trace stage, so which piece it is has become the useful question -- though the stage itself is now ~5 s of demo3, so the answer is information for M3.1's cost model rather than a target.

host_synchronizations_in_the_trace_loop.bounded_above_by: `repository_side_handoff`, which contains it -- so the synchronization cannot be more than 2.5% of the as-committed chunk however much of that stage it turns out to be
host_synchronizations_in_the_trace_loop.disposition: kept, and justified rather than removed. It reads one scalar -- the clipped-ray count -- which demo3's energy ledger consumes per chunk as `invalid_rays` to separate an aperture loss from an empty draw. Nothing else in the loop reads a device value to the host, and no shape in it is data-dependent, so there is no synchronization of the kind CHE-101 found costing 49 s in the reconstruction.
host_synchronizations_in_the_trace_loop.marginal_reduction_note: the reduction and host read, timed on the traced `valid` array once the trace's own work has drained. It is a LOWER bound on what the synchronization costs in place, where it may also wait on outstanding device work.

requested.device_note: optiland 0.6.0 set_device takes 'cpu' or 'cuda' only; the physical GPU is selected by the container's visible devices

per_ray_cost_model.note: the as-shipped figure is the one to plan against; the as-committed figure is what every demo3 record before this issue was paying. Both are fp32 on the environment fingerprint above, and neither is portable off it.

record.label: optiland_trace_decomposition_200000rays_fp32

memory_report.signal_rationale: container cgroup swap, not host swap: host swap is non-zero at rest on this machine (CHE-64), so a host-swap delta is not attributable to this run

notes: Each arm is itself a median of synchronized repeats chosen from a 1 s budget; `measurement` here times the three arms together and is not the figure to quote.

detail.arms: per-ray wavelength array, size-1 wavelength array, shipped call

why_the_remainder_is_zero: the three contributions are differences between measured arms and therefore partition the reconstructed total exactly, so a zero remainder here is arithmetic and not evidence. The two things that ARE evidence: `closure_against_committed_record`, which checks the reconstructed total against the 98.96 s this profile claims to decompose, and `independent_estimate_ratio`, which reproduces the dominant contribution from a separate measurement of the material lookups it is made of.
